standard_prerequisites.name: Splitting of an idempotent endomorphism
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the direct sum decomposition of an object on which an idempotent and its complement act, which is applied to the composite of the two given morphisms.

standard_prerequisites.name: The kernel and cokernel of a split endomorphism
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the identification of the first given morphism as the kernel and of the second as the cokernel of the endomorphism, which is what turns the abstract decomposition into the displayed one.

core_obligations: The idempotent (proof line 714): writing f for the composite of the two given morphisms, the author computes that f composed with itself is f, so the composite is idempotent and the previous lemma applies to it.

The decomposition (proof lines 715-718): applying the splitting lemma to the idempotent and the two remaining lemmas therefore produces the displayed direct sum decompositions of the source into the kernel and the cokernel of that endomorphism together with the target, with the structure maps as described.
proof_roadmap: Check that the composite of the two given morphisms is idempotent.
Apply the splitting lemma to that idempotent.
Identify the kernel and cokernel of the composite with the two given morphisms.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for a pair of morphisms j and q with q j the identity, if the composite j q has a kernel or a cokernel then both exist and the source splits as the kernel of the composite plus the target, and likewise with the cokernel, with the structure of the direct sum determined by the given morphisms (statement lines 696-712). The proof is a complete argument: the composite is shown to be idempotent by a direct computation, and the splitting lemma applied to that idempotent, together with the lemma identifying the kernel and cokernel of the composite with the two given morphisms, yields the displayed decompositions (proof lines 714-718). The non-formal content is the computation of the idempotent. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
